$ front --help
--- stdout
usage: front [-h] [--project SLUG] {visits,leads,doctor} ...

front — the front door of patchlamp.com: who came, and who left a number.
Patchlamp plan 06 (ROADMAP B2). The site counts its own page loads with no
cookie (a beacon per load; a hash that changes daily) and stores every
"leave your number". This reads both back, for Taylor in the terminal or
for Patch on the global project when Taylor texts "how's the front door".

  front                      # the week: visits by day, top pages, referrers, new leads
  front visits [--days 7]    # visits by day, top pages, top referring sites
  front leads [--all]        # the leads (new ones only unless --all)
  front --project SLUG       # a client's own site instead (B127): page loads by day, pages, referrers
  front doctor

`--project` is Taylor's view of any client site's count (plan
~/projects/plans/50-site-numbers.md); inside a client workspace the same
numbers are `site stats`, which can only read that workspace's own.

Talks to patchlamp.com's /internal/relay/front/* with the relay's shared
secret. Read-only: telling Taylor about a lead is the relay's job
(relay/front.py), which marks each one told on the site.

Config, by name, never printed:
  PATCHLAMP_RELAY_SHARED_SECRET   ~/.config/claude-tools/env
  PATCHLAMP_URL                   optional; default https://patchlamp.com

positional arguments:
  {visits,leads,doctor}
    visits              visits by day, top pages, top referring sites
    leads               who left a number (new ones unless --all)
    doctor              can this reach the site?

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --project SLUG        a client's own site instead of patchlamp.com (B127)
--- stderr
--- exit 0
